title_en: A travel diary with the San Francisco 49ers
teaser_en: Almost 70 49ers fans from Germany on the NEG group trip: tailgating, a Monday night win at Levi's Stadium, a stadium tour and a sideline conversation about the 49ers' presence in Germany.
body_en:
*…and the chances of a bigger presence in Germany*

It is Monday, October 26, 2026, and I am sitting on the plane from Atlanta back to Frankfurt with a big grin on my face. Over the past nine days, almost 70 49ers fans from Germany got an intimate look inside the historic San Francisco 49ers franchise.

## The group trip of The Niner Empire Germany e.V.

For four years now, the German chapter of The Niner Empire movement has been organizing group trips to the 49ers in the USA. The concept: right after the schedule release in May, one home game and one to three road games per season are selected, and thanks to by now good contacts with the San Francisco 49ers, group tickets without service fees are offered for various sections at the home game. That saves many 49ers fans from Germany a lot of money, and they end up sitting together in large groups at Levi's Stadium. Everyone books the rest of the trip on their own, and the travelers help each other with choosing hotels and flights and with any other questions that come up. Besides the home game against the Washington Commanders, the road games at the Atlanta Falcons, the Dallas Cowboys and the New York Giants were also selected to bring more 49ers fans from Germany together at the games.

## Activities, tailgating and the stadium visit

On the eve of the Monday night game against the Washington Commanders, around 60 travelers met at a spot near the 49ers' old facility in Redwood City. The "Canyon Inn" is like a 49ers museum. Back in the '80s, owner Tim Harrison regularly served breakfast to players like Joe Montana, Dwight Clark and Keena Turner, and he fascinated everyone with lots of stories and a historic interior.

On game day, the large travel group met on the Green Lot at Levi's Stadium 3.5 hours before kickoff for an intense tailgating experience. Booming bass, Mexican bands, brief encounters with former tight end Delanie Walker and the rappers P-Lo and E-40, food and drinks of every kind and lots of good conversations made for complete sensory overload for everyone involved, even before the game. The travel group was approached again and again by passing 49ers fans and celebrated for their wanderlust from Germany. It is always fascinating to see how overwhelmed 49ers fans from Germany are when, for the first time in their lives, they are standing in front of their favorite team's living room, savoring every single second.

![The NEG travel group tailgating on the Green Lot, with Levi's Stadium in the background](https://i0.wp.com/theninerempiregermany.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/reisekolumne-tailgate-scaled.jpg?resize=1440%2C2560&ssl=1)

*The NEG travel group tailgating on the Green Lot, with Levi's Stadium in the background.*

Equipped with field passes, a very small delegation was allowed onto the hallowed turf of Levi's Stadium before the game, where they experienced the pregame rituals of the families of Brock Purdy, George Kittle, Kyle Juszczyk and Christian McCaffrey up close and watched the players warm up from just a few feet away.

## Will we soon see the 49ers with a bigger presence in Germany?

Before the game, representatives of The Niner Empire Germany e.V. (NEG) used the opportunity on the sideline to talk with 49ers Chief Marketing Officer Stephanie Rogers and Senior Manager Brand Marketing Laurence Scott about the San Francisco 49ers' international market. In the conversation, Stephanie Rogers made clear that teams have no influence on taking part in the NFL International Games, or on a game in Germany in particular. Niner Empire Germany, however, made it very clear that tens of thousands of 49ers fans in Germany would be delighted to see a bigger presence on the ground.

Asked whether, after the United Kingdom, Mexico and the United Arab Emirates, the 49ers would apply next for the marketing rights in Germany through the NFL Global Markets Program, Rogers answered: "Not yet."

With eleven teams, Germany is already the country with the most NFL teams holding marketing rights: the Atlanta Falcons, Carolina Panthers, Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers, Indianapolis Colts, Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots, New York Giants, Pittsburgh Steelers, Seattle Seahawks and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

In the end, the San Francisco 49ers won the game 23-17. After a very strong first half with three offensive touchdowns, the 49ers made it exciting again after wide receiver Mike Evans got hurt. The travel group experienced a lively and loud Levi's Stadium at a Monday Night Football game whose noise forced opposing quarterback Jayden Daniels into at least one timeout and one mistake. Night games have a very special charm, and not only at Levi's Stadium: during the game you can see the beautiful orange sunset over the Bay Area, the crowd is much more electric than at day games, and Levi's Stadium with its new video walls and light installations also comes into its own in a completely different way after dark.

![Sunset over the Bay Area](https://i0.wp.com/theninerempiregermany.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/reisekolumne-sonnenuntergang.jpg?resize=1366%2C2048&ssl=1)

![Aerial view of a night game at Levi's Stadium](https://i0.wp.com/theninerempiregermany.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/reisekolumne-nightgame-luftaufnahme-scaled-e1793356799268.jpg?resize=1600%2C901&ssl=1)

*Sunset and floodlights over the Bay Area: the special charm of a night game at Levi's Stadium.*

## A tour of Levi's Stadium

Another highlight for all travelers every year is the stadium tour on the day after the game. Because of Levi's Stadium's location in the South Bay in Santa Clara, the 49ers do not offer commercial stadium tours, so the tour for the NEG is the only big stadium tour of the year. After a short welcome from Laurence Scott, all participants received a George Kittle bobblehead to mark his tenth anniversary with the 49ers. This was followed by a look at the suite level, the press box and the stadium's catacombs. The press box at Levi's Stadium is the largest of its kind in the NFL. The travel group was also allowed onto the edge of the field, where the 49ers had fought for their next win the night before.

![View from the suite level of Levi's Stadium](https://i0.wp.com/theninerempiregermany.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/reisekolumne-suite-level-scaled.jpg?resize=1440%2C2560&ssl=1)

*View from the suite level of Levi's Stadium during the exclusive NEG stadium tour.*

After the stadium tour, some travelers headed back home, others used the time for a few days off in the Bay Area, and around 15 people flew on during the week to the road game at the Atlanta Falcons and to a Southeastern Conference college football game, the Alabama Crimson Tide against Texas A&M. Group trips with The Niner Empire Germany e.V. not only bring 49ers fans of all ages to a San Francisco 49ers game for the first time, but over the past four years have also created many special moments and friendships.

![The whole travel group on the field at Levi's Stadium](https://i0.wp.com/theninerempiregermany.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/reisekolumne-stadiontour-gruppe-scaled.jpg?resize=1600%2C900&ssl=1)

*The whole travel group on the field at Levi's Stadium: faithful to the Bay.*

As the organizer of these trips and the author of this piece, I would like to sincerely thank everyone who traveled with us this year for another unforgettable and intense time, and I am already looking forward to the years to come.

Go Niners!

David Rösler
